title: PowerToys general settings lost on every restart unless manually exited from tray
summary: Two reporters show that normal Windows session-ending can leave General settings as an empty object while tray Exit preserves them, and public source history identifies a shutdown-specific cleanup path plus an unguarded final settings rewrite that need focused design and reproduction.

judgment.rationale: The issue is reproducible across multiple systems and distinguishes normal session-ending from tray Exit with before/after logs. Current Runner code treats WM_ENDSESSION as a fast shutdown path, skips blocking Settings and Quick Access cleanup, then writes get_general_settings().to_json() directly to settings.json when the message loop returns normally. The public evidence proves an empty object is persisted during the prior shutdown, but does not yet identify which shutdown-time writer or state transition produces the empty snapshot. A focused design can add writer attribution, reject destructive empty snapshots, and make the final commit atomic without reintroducing the APPLICATION_HANG_QUIESCE regression that motivated the fast shutdown path.
evidence: The original reporter reproduced the loss after normal shutdown/restart and graceful WM_CLOSE, but not after tray Exit.
The original reporter confirmed settings.json was already empty before relaunch when Run at startup was disabled.

A second reporter reproduced the same behavior on a personal PC and a managed laptop and supplied a runner log showing populated settings before WM_DESTROY with system_session_ending=true and apply_general_settings: {} on the next launch.
Merged PR #48363 introduced the system-session-ending path that skips close_settings_window and QuickAccessHost::stop to avoid APPLICATION_HANG_QUIESCE.
runner/main.cpp still calls PTSettingsHelper::save_general_settings(get_general_settings().to_json()) after a normal message-loop return.
PTSettingsHelper::save_general_settings writes directly through json::to_file without a non-empty snapshot guard or an atomic replace contract.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused shutdown-persistence design and run the supplied maintainer reproduction to identify the writer/state transition before implementing the guard and atomic commit.

fix_assessment.rationale: The corruption occurs in PowerToys-owned Runner and settings persistence paths, no covering fix is linked, and the public source exposes concrete shutdown and file-write boundaries suitable for a targeted fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve the last validated General settings snapshot during session-ending shutdown
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The system-session-ending path can reach the unconditional final General settings write with an empty or incomplete in-memory snapshot while concurrent shutdown cleanup is intentionally skipped; the direct json::to_file call then replaces a previously valid settings.json with that destructive snapshot.
plan: Instrument every General settings writer with a public-safe source identifier, session-ending state, and payload shape so the WM_ENDSESSION reproduction identifies which writer emits the empty object.
Capture and retain the last successfully loaded or saved non-empty General settings snapshot in the Runner before entering the message loop.
At shutdown, reject an empty/default snapshot that would replace a previously valid file unless the write is tied to an explicit user reset operation.
Replace direct destructive writes with a temp-file write, parse/read-back validation, and atomic replace that preserves the prior settings.json on failure.
Keep the fast WM_ENDSESSION path non-blocking: perform one bounded synchronous final commit from the validated snapshot and do not restore the cross-process waits removed by PR #48363.
Add regression tests for tray Exit, external WM_CLOSE, confirmed WM_ENDSESSION, a simulated empty shutdown snapshot, and atomic-write failure.
verification: Run the issue's normal restart/shutdown reproduction repeatedly and confirm settings.json remains populated before the next PowerToys launch.
Run graceful taskkill /IM PowerToys.exe without /F and confirm General settings persist.
Confirm writer-attribution logs identify exactly one accepted final write and no rejected valid user reset.
Run focused common JSON/settings tests and Runner session-end tests, including preservation of the prior file after a failed temp-file validation or replace.
Verify tray Exit remains unchanged and the shutdown path does not regress APPLICATION_HANG_QUIESCE.

confidence.rationale: The shutdown boundary, destructive final write, and cross-machine reproduction are well supported, but a targeted trace is still needed to confirm which writer or state transition supplies the empty snapshot.

issue_context.summary: General settings are intermittently replaced by an empty object during non-tray shutdown paths, with a second independent report corroborating the same WM_DESTROY session-ending sequence.
known_information: The original report uses PowerToys v0.101.2362 and Windows 11 25H2 and reproduces across user and system installation scopes.
Increasing Windows shutdown timeouts, changing elevation, disabling startup, and checking AV/EDR did not prevent the loss.
Tray Exit consistently preserves settings, while normal shutdown and graceful external WM_CLOSE can corrupt them.
The second reporter reproduced on two machines and attached a runner log with populated settings before session ending and an empty object on the next launch.
Current Runner code skips selected cleanup during confirmed system session ending and performs a final General settings save after the message loop returns.
No assignee, linked fix PR, or duplicate currently owns the behavioral fix.
inferences: The regression boundary may involve the shutdown cleanup changes from PR #48363, but the public evidence does not prove that commit alone creates the empty snapshot.
The final unguarded save makes an empty in-memory snapshot destructive even if another component or state transition is responsible for producing it.
A safe fix must preserve the quiesce-time improvement while preventing invalid snapshots from replacing the last valid file.
issue_context.analysis: The report now has independent corroboration and exact log sequencing, so asking the reporters for generic diagnostics would not reduce uncertainty. The remaining discriminator is maintainer-side tracing of the finite General settings write sites during WM_ENDSESSION. The design should therefore combine writer attribution, a validated last-known-good snapshot, an explicit-empty/reset distinction, and atomic persistence.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, all three comments, labels, assignees, attachment references, and latest corroborating log excerpt.
Inspected runner/tray_icon.cpp session-end handling, runner/main.cpp final save, runner/general_settings.cpp write sites, and common/SettingsAPI/settings_helpers.cpp.
Traced the system_session_ending cleanup behavior to merged PR #48363 and confirmed the unconditional final save predates that change.
Searched upstream issues and PRs for settings.json shutdown loss and found no linked active fix for this exact corruption.

actions.label: Approve shutdown-safe General settings design

design.title: Preserve validated General settings during WM_ENDSESSION
design.prompt: Design a focused fix for PowerToys issue #50616 using the public reproduction and source evidence. Trace every General settings writer during confirmed WM_ENDSESSION; retain the last validated non-empty snapshot; distinguish an explicit user reset from an accidental empty/default shutdown snapshot; write through a validated temporary file and atomic replace; keep the shutdown path bounded and non-blocking so PR #48363's APPLICATION_HANG_QUIESCE fix is preserved; and add regression coverage for tray Exit, WM_CLOSE, WM_ENDSESSION, empty snapshots, and failed replacement.

actions.note: Approval starts fork-side design work only; no upstream write occurs automatically.

reproduce.version_requirement: v0.101.2362.0 or a current build before the shutdown-persistence fix
prerequisites: A test account with at least one General setting and module-enabled state changed from defaults.
A diagnostic build that logs each General settings write source, payload key count, system_session_ending state, and success without logging sensitive values.
Run at startup disabled for the before-relaunch file check.
steps: Start PowerToys, change a General setting and at least one module-enabled state, and verify settings.json is populated.
Restart Windows normally without using tray Exit.
Before relaunching PowerToys, inspect settings.json and correlate its final modification with the attributed write records.
Repeat using taskkill /IM PowerToys.exe without /F to exercise WM_CLOSE.
Repeat using tray Exit as the known-good control.
If corruption occurs, record which writer attempted the empty snapshot and whether the prior valid snapshot was still available.
reproduce.expected_result: The trace identifies the shutdown-time writer/state transition, settings.json remains a populated valid object after every path, and the Runner exits within the Windows quiesce budget.

author: Maximilian-Siegl-zh-tech

related_prs.relationship: Introduced the current fast system-session-ending cleanup path and is a relevant regression boundary, not a confirmed covering fix.

upstream_safety.detail: No comments, labels, assignments, closures, or other public mutations were made to microsoft/PowerToys.
